Required and safe; dose usually needs increasing
TSH (and free T4) periodically; 4-8 weeks after dose change
summary: Levothyroxine (synthetic T4) is the treatment of choice for hypothyroidism and for TSH suppression in thyroid cancer/nodules. It is a narrow-therapeutic-index drug requiring consistent administration on an empty stomach and TSH-guided titration. It carries a boxed warning against use for obesity/weight loss. Doses must be lower and titrated slowly in the elderly and those with cardiac disease.
indications: Hypothyroidism (primary, secondary, tertiary) of any cause
Pituitary TSH suppression in thyroid nodules and thyroid cancer
Adjunct in management of well-differentiated thyroid cancer

dosage.d: Approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day once daily; titrate by 12.5-25 mcg every 4-6 weeks
Start 12.5-25 mcg once daily; titrate slowly
dosage.n: Increase cautiously to avoid cardiac strain
Check TSH each trimester / soon after confirming pregnancy

dosage.d: Start 12.5-25 mcg once daily and titrate slowly
Age/weight based (e.g., infants 10-15 mcg/kg/day, decreasing with age)
dosage.n: Critical for neurodevelopment; do not interrupt

admin: Take once daily on an empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before breakfast, with a full glass of water
Take at least 4 hours apart from interfering products (calcium, iron, antacids, bile-acid binders)
Be consistent with brand/product - bioequivalence varies
Stop biotin supplements at least 2 days before thyroid lab tests
moa: Synthetic levothyroxine (T4) is converted peripherally to the active T3, which binds nuclear thyroid hormone receptors to regulate gene transcription. This increases metabolic rate, protein synthesis, growth/development, and cardiovascular and CNS function, replacing endogenous thyroid hormone.

absolute: Uncorrected adrenal insufficiency (treat first - risk of acute adrenal crisis)
Acute myocardial infarction without hypothyroid cause
monitor: Bone density with long-term suppressive doses

preg: Required and safe in pregnancy - maternal hypothyroidism harms the fetus. Levothyroxine requirements usually increase; check TSH as soon as pregnancy is confirmed and each trimester, adjusting to trimester-specific targets.
lact: Compatible with breastfeeding; only minimal amounts pass into milk. Adequate maternal thyroid hormone supports normal lactation.
renal: No specific dose adjustment required for renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment required for hepatic impairment.

moderate: Calcium, iron, antacids, sucralfate, bile-acid sequestrants, phosphate binders (reduce absorption - separate by 4 hours)
Estrogens (increased thyroid-binding globulin - higher dose needs)
Enzyme inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin - increased clearance)
minor: Soy products and high-fiber meals (reduced absorption)
Biotin (lab assay interference, not true effect)
interactions.food: Food, coffee, soy, fiber, and calcium reduce absorption - take on an empty stomach
interactions.diagnostics: Biotin can falsely alter thyroid immunoassays; affects TSH/T4 interpretation

common: Generally none at correct dose (side effects reflect over- or under-treatment)
serious: Over-treatment: palpitations, tachyarrhythmia/atrial fibrillation, angina, MI
Accelerated bone loss/osteoporosis with chronic over-replacement
Precipitation of adrenal crisis if coexisting untreated adrenal insufficiency
emergency: Cardiac arrhythmia / acute coronary event from over-dose
Adrenal crisis (if adrenal insufficiency not treated first)

monitoring: TSH (and free T4 where relevant) - recheck 4-8 weeks after any dose change, then periodically
Free T4/TSH each trimester in pregnancy
Cardiac symptoms during initiation/titration in older or cardiac patients
Bone mineral density with long-term TSH-suppressive therapy
counsel: Take at the same time every day, on an empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before breakfast
Separate from calcium, iron, and antacids by at least 4 hours
Do not switch brands without telling your doctor; recheck TSH after a switch
This is lifelong therapy for most patients - do not stop without advice
Report palpitations, chest pain, heat intolerance, tremor, or weight loss (signs of too much)
pk: Clinical effect gradual over days to weeks; metabolic effects build slowly
Serum T4 peaks ~2-4 hours after dosing
Long - supports stable once-daily dosing; peak therapeutic effect may take 4-6 weeks
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Narrow therapeutic index - titrate by TSH, not symptoms alone, and keep to a consistent product
Boxed warning: not for obesity or weight loss; large doses can be life-threatening
Long ~7-day half-life means dose changes take ~6 weeks to fully reflect in TSH
Always treat coexisting adrenal insufficiency before starting to avoid adrenal crisis
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember that day. If you forget for a whole day, you may take two doses the next day (the long half-life makes this safe) unless told otherwise by your doctor.
overdose: Acute or chronic overdose causes thyrotoxic features: tachycardia, arrhythmia, tremor, agitation, hyperthermia, and, in severe cases, thyroid storm. Management is supportive with beta-blockers for cardiac/adrenergic symptoms and reduction/withholding of the dose; effects may be delayed due to the long half-life.
